questions.title: Why does block quantization reduce numerical error in FP8 FlashAttention-3?
questions.question_body: The paper claims that block quantization (using one scale per block rather than per tensor) reduces the RMSE of FP8 attention by up to 2.6× compared to per‑tensor scaling. I understand that outliers cause large quantization errors, but how exactly does using a separate scale per block help? Does this simply lower the dynamic range per block, or is there a deeper interaction with the attention weighting that I’m missing?

questions.title: How does incoherent processing with a random orthogonal matrix preserve attention scores?
questions.question_body: The authors multiply both Q and K by a random orthogonal matrix M before quantizing, claiming that Q M × (K M)^T = Q K^T. Can someone provide a step‑by‑step derivation of this identity for the case where M is constructed from a Hadamard matrix and random ±1 diagonals? I’m also curious about any numerical stability implications of performing this multiplication in FP8.

questions.title: What are the layout constraints for FP8 WGMMA on Hopper?
questions.question_body: The paper mentions that for FP8 WGMMA only k‑major input operands are accepted, whereas FP16 accepts both mn‑major and k‑major. Could you explain how this restriction arises from the underlying Tensor Core datapath? Also, how do we reconcile the distinct layouts of the FP32 accumulator and the FP8 operand when chaining two successive WGMMA operations in FlashAttention‑3?

questions.title: "Pingpong" scheduling: what barriers synchronize and why?
questions.question_body: In the description of the overlapping GEMM–softmax pipeline, two warp groups are said to ping‑pong by swapping roles every iteration. The paper references `bar.sync` barriers but doesn’t detail which specific operations are preordered by them. Which WGMMA invocations must finish before the exponential operations begin, and how does this ordering avoid hazards if the compiler reorders instructions?

questions.title: Is LDSM/STSM capable of transposing packed FP8 tiles efficiently?
questions.question_body: The implementation relies on LDSM/STSM instructions to transpose V tiles in kernel while loading from global memory. The PTX manual describes these as 8×8 matrices with 16‑bit entries; for 8‑bit entries we need to pack two values together. How exactly do we perform the bit‑packing/unpacking without loss of precision, and what register movements are required to achieve an exact transpose of an 8‑bit tile?

questions.title: "Producer–consumer" warp–specialization: how are registers allocated across warps?
questions.question_body: The algorithm splits warps into producers and consumers, using `setmaxnreg` to allocate registers differently. How is the number of registers per warp decided given different tile sizes and head dimensions? What happens if too many warps need registers – do we get register spilling or do we have to reduce tile size?

questions.title: "Two‑stage" WGMMA–softmax pipelining: when can we overlap softmax with the next GEMM?
questions.question_body: In Algorithm 2, after computing S_cur = Q_i K_j^T we immediately compute m_i, Ptilde_cur and l_i before proceeding to S_next. Are there any hidden dependencies that prevent overlapping this softmax operation with the GEMM computation of S_next? What conditions on B_r, B_c or on GPU resource availability guarantee that such pipelining does not stall?

questions.title: "Three‑stage" pipelining: why doesn’t it always give higher throughput?
questions.question_body: "Three stages" would theoretically overlap more operations but requires extra registers. In practice why might increasing stages beyond two lead to diminishing returns or even degrade performance? Is it solely reg pressure or also instruction scheduling or memory bandwidth limits?

questions.title: "Warp specialisation" vs. classic threadblock parallelism: is there any performance penalty for splitting warps into producers/consumers?
questions.question_body: By assigning only one thread per producer warp for TMA loads (as hinted), doesn’t this underutilize thread resources compared to a fully parallel load strategy? How does this trade‑off pan out empirically on H100 for small sequence lengths?

questions.title: "Softmax realscaling" after accumulation: why is diag(exp(m_old − m)) applied only at certain points?
questions.question_body: In Algorithm 1 we compute 	ilde{P}_i^{(j)} = exp(S_i^{(j)}−m_i) and later rescale O_i with diag(exp(m_old−m)). Could someone walk me through why we must maintain an explicit `m_i` update across all blocks, rather than just using a per‑block maximum? Does this affect numerical stability when sequence length is large?

questions.title: "Quantization error" analysis: do outliers truly dominate error in FP8 when using incoherent processing?
questions.question_body: A quantitative bound would be helpful: given a normal distribution with variance σ² plus occasional outliers with variance (10 σ)² at probability p=0.001, can we estimate linearly how much error is contributed by outliers under per‑tensor scaling versus block scaling? I’d like to understand why incoherent processing further helps even once block scaling is used.
